facts.fact: Research from the Video Advertising Bureau suggests CTV ads typically need 3 to 5 exposures to drive measurable action.
facts.quote: Research from the Video Advertising Bureau suggests that CTV ads typically need 3 to 5 exposures to drive measurable action.

facts.fact: The page states that CTV completion rates typically run 90% or higher because viewers can't skip the ads.
facts.quote: CTV completion rates typically run 90% or higher because viewers can't skip the ads.

facts.fact: The page states that skip rates for pre-roll video ads on YouTube often exceed 70%.
facts.quote: Compare this to pre-roll video ads on YouTube, where skip rates often exceed 70%.

facts.fact: The page states that typical CPMs for small business CTV campaigns range from $15 to $35, with $25 a common average.
facts.quote: For small business CTV campaigns, typical CPMs range from $15 to $35, with $25 being a common average.

facts.fact: The page recommends a sustained increase of 20% or more in branded searches as a strong signal that TV advertising is working.
facts.quote: A sustained increase of 20% or more in branded searches is a strong signal.

facts.fact: The page recommends recording baseline metrics for at least 4 weeks before a CTV campaign starts.
facts.quote: Record your current branded search volume, website traffic, phone call volume, and new customer counts for at least 4 weeks before the campaign starts.

facts.fact: The page recommends measuring key metrics for 4 to 8 weeks before launching a CTV campaign for before/after comparison.
facts.quote: measure your key metrics for 4 to 8 weeks before launching your CTV campaign

facts.fact: The page suggests geo-based tests can take about 90 days before comparing new customer growth between markets.
facts.quote: After 90 days, compare new customer growth, branded search trends, and revenue between the two markets.

facts.fact: The page recommends running incremental lift on/off tests only after the campaign has run for at least 60 days.
facts.quote: Best done after the campaign has been running for at least 60 days.

facts.fact: The page recommends pausing a CTV campaign for two weeks in an on/off incremental lift test.
facts.quote: Pause your CTV campaign for two weeks, then restart it.

facts.fact: The page states the article was published on March 9, 2026.
Adwave states that realistic branded search lift for small business CTV campaigns is 20 to 40% increase during active campaigns.
facts.quote: **Branded search lift:** 20 to 40% increase during active campaigns. Some businesses see even higher lifts.

facts.fact: Adwave states that realistic website traffic lift for small business CTV campaigns is a 15 to 30% increase in direct and organic traffic.
facts.quote: **Website traffic lift:** 15 to 30% increase in direct and organic traffic.

facts.fact: Adwave states that cost per thousand impressions for local targeting in small business CTV campaigns is $15 to $35.
facts.quote: **Cost per thousand impressions:** $15 to $35 for local targeting.

facts.fact: Adwave states that completion rates of 90% or higher are realistic for 30-second non-skippable CTV ads.
facts.quote: **Completion rates:** 90% or higher for 30-second non-skippable ads.

facts.fact: Adwave states to expect 10 to 25% of new customers to mention TV/streaming as a discovery channel in surveys, while noting actual influence is likely higher.
facts.quote: **New customer attribution:** Expect 10 to 25% of new customers to mention TV/streaming as a discovery channel in surveys

facts.fact: Adwave states most small businesses see measurable brand lift in 30 to 60 days, and clear ROI attribution typically takes 60 to 90 days of consistent campaigning.
facts.value: 30 to 60 days (brand lift); 60 to 90 days (ROI attribution)
facts.quote: Most small businesses see measurable brand lift in 30 to 60 days. Clear ROI attribution typically takes 60 to 90 days of consistent campaigning.

facts.fact: Adwave advises establishing at least 4 weeks of baseline data before a TV campaign goes live.
facts.quote: Always establish at least 4 weeks of baseline data before your campaign goes live.

facts.fact: Adwave states that for most local markets, a minimum of $500 to $1,000 per month for at least 60 to 90 days is needed to measure TV advertising effectiveness.
facts.quote: For most local markets, that means running at a minimum of $500 to $1,000 per month for at least 60 to 90 days.

facts.fact: Adwave lists a $30-a-day starting point for its campaigns.
facts.quote: With [Adwave's $30-a-day starting point](https://adwave.com/pricing), you can test the creative and platform

facts.fact: Adwave states QR code scan rates on CTV are typically low, at 1 to 3% of viewers.
facts.quote: scan rates on CTV are typically low (1 to 3% of viewers)

facts.fact: Adwave states a dedicated landing page URL captures 100% attributable TV-driven web visits, but will undercount because most viewers won't remember a specific URL.
facts.quote: the visits you do capture are 100% attributable.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends reviewing platform metrics weekly and business outcome metrics bi-weekly or monthly.
facts.quote: Review platform metrics (impressions, reach, frequency) weekly. Check business outcome metrics (branded searches, website traffic, leads) bi-weekly or monthly.

facts.fact: Adwave recommends running a monthly attribution report and reviewing it after three months to see clear trends.
facts.quote: After three months, you'll have enough data points to see clear trends and make confident budget decisions.
